extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants, nominators, and regional Ford staff involved in the Ford Global Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for nomination, application, and selection of Ford Global Fellowship candidates—covering who is eligible, what qualities and commitments Fellows should have, and the nomination/selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on addressing root causes of inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Proximate to and directly engaged in addressing inequality: Fellows must be leading work that is intentionally focused on addressing the root causes of inequality and tackling problems at the systemic level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows should be advancing justice and addressing systemic drivers of inequality; work need not align exactly with Ford's current grant-making priorities and may be interdisciplinary or intersectional (e.g., land rights + civic engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated meaningful impact but unrealized potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should have demonstrated meaningful impact, but whose full potential has yet to be fully realized because of a lack of resources or access to a global network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors leaders who have a track record of impact and are positioned to increase their future impact if given resources and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of approaches and cohort composition
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not one archetype: the Fellowship seeks a diverse cohort so Fellows can learn from one another and generate fresh thinking on addressing inequality across borders and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cohort should include a wide diversity of approaches, sectors, and ways of thinking; some Fellows may have cross-regional experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical leadership and visible integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be ethical individuals, lead with visible integrity, and act with morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are expected to embody integrity in leadership, including humility and responsible public visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity and openness to learning beyond current sphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be profoundly curious to expand their perspectives beyond their current sphere of concern and demonstrate openness to learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show a willingness to learn from others, engage across contexts, and pursue new perspectives as part of the Community of Practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of leadership skills (creativity, strategy, dedication, humility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows will have a combination of skills including creativity, strategic thinking, dedication, humility, and deep curiosity about learning with other leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection considers these leadership competencies alongside demonstrated impact and potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poised to benefit: mid-career with track record and future potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows will have both a demonstrated meaningful track record and be positioned for future impact; broadly 'mid-career' and at an inflection point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program targets individuals who have prior success but clear potential for greater impact, not early-career novices or those already fully established globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatively under-resourced and under-networked
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for candidates who are relatively under-resourced and under-networked, such that the Fellowship's resources and network would materially expand their impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not disqualifying, candidates who already have robust global networks and resources are less likely to be a fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness and ability to commit to program time and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be committed to the time and requirements of the Fellowship, including full, active, and engaged participation in three week-long in-person gatherings and regular virtual cohort experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must commit to participating in all multi-day gatherings and monthly virtual cohort connection activities during their Fellowship period; failure to commit may affect selection or standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Learning Plan engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are expected to pursue an Individual Learning Plan and engage approximately 4–6 hours each month on related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option to work with a leadership coach; ILP activities are part of expected monthly engagement during the Fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of Practice co-creation and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows will actively co-create the Community of Practice with the Foundation, including refining learning agendas, sharing insights, supporting others' learning, and participating in reflection and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows share responsibility for creating a supportive, collaborative community during and after the Fellowship and may be asked to host regional conversations, nominate future Fellows, or mentor others.

rubrics_metrics.name: English proficiency or demonstrated path to proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: All Fellowship programming will be conducted in English; candidates who demonstrate they are on a path to proficiency may be considered but must be willing to pursue proficiency in both written and spoken English by the start of the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated willingness and concrete plan toward English fluency required if not already proficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic eligibility: reside/work in participating Ford regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows should live and/or work in one of the 11 participating regions or countries where the Ford Foundation has a presence (United States; Brazil; Andean Region; Mexico and Central America; India, Sri Lanka and Nepal; Eastern Africa; West Africa; Southern Africa; Middle East and North Africa; Indonesia; China).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not a residential program and Fellows do not need to move; work may span multiple countries or regions. Regional Ford teams review nominations for eligibility and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may come from a wide range of sectors, including public, private, civil society, artists, and academics; some Fellows may be unaffiliated or work across sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellowship seeks the best candidates regardless of sector or organizational affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination required
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be nominated: Ford receives nominations from selected nominators based on the selection considerations for the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators are identified by Ford's regional offices and the Fellowship team to expand beyond usual networks; nominators may choose whether to tell nominees they are being nominated. Foundation staff will contact qualified nominees to invite applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: four-step review and reference checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection follows four steps: Nomination; Application (regional Ford team reviews nominations and invites candidates to apply); Regional Interview (regional team reviews applications and may invite virtual interview); Global Interview (selected candidates invited to virtual global interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates advancing to the global interview stage will be expected to submit two references that will be checked as part of due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: current government officials in elective or appointive public office
rubrics_metrics.description: Current government officials in an elective or appointive public office are not eligible to be Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who work in the government sector but are not current office-holders may be eligible; ensure status at selection time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: under 18 and political candidates during term
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be over age 18. Candidates for a political office chosen through a partisan election, either currently or during the Fellowship term, cannot be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age and political candidacy status are hard eligibility limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility: Ford staff and family members
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford staff and their family members are not eligible for the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People affiliated with Ford Foundation grantees or prior Ford Fellows may apply, but the program expects most Fellows will not be affiliated with current/former grantees or be prior Fellowship beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference against prior fellowship beneficiaries or highly networked leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: While not an absolute disqualification, the Fellowship is not looking primarily for people who are already well-established with robust global networks and resources, or those who have been beneficiaries of other fellowship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to reach leaders who are under-resourced and who will materially benefit from the Fellowship's network and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility: reasonable accommodations for applicants and Fellows with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will provide reasonable accommodations deemed necessary for qualified candidates and Fellows to participate in the selection process and in the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate accommodation needs so the Foundation can support full participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to be publicly visible and mindful of personal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Fellowship is a high-profile initiative; potential applicants should be mindful that visibility can bring opportunity and potential personal risk for those advocating for certain populations or working on contentious issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be willing to be visible at the global level and consider personal safety implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scale and stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation intends to support approximately 200 Fellows over an initial ten-year commitment; each Fellow will receive a US$25,000 stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation will also cover all travel costs associated with the Fellowship's convenings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics: travel costs covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Foundation will cover all travel costs associated with the Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are not expected to pay travel costs to convenings.
